findings.description: The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true, giving it a public endpoint reachable from the internet rather than confining it to the VPC. Combined with a well-known master username ('admin') and no storage encryption, this exposes the database directly to credential-guessing and exploitation from untrusted networks.
storage_encrypted = false disables KMS encryption of the RDS volume, automated snapshots and backups, so all catalog data is stored in cleartext on AWS-managed media.

The user_data script interpolates the RDS master username and var.password directly into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc. EC2 user data is retrievable unauthenticated from the instance metadata service (169.254.169.254/latest/user-data) by any process or SSRF vector on the host, and is also visible to anyone with ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute, leaking the database master password.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*". Any compromise of the web application yields full control of all S3 buckets, EC2 (including launching instances and passing/modifying network config) and RDS in the account — a clear privilege-escalation and data-exfiltration path from a publicly reachable host.

No metadata_options block is specified, so the instance defaults to allowing IMDSv1 (http_tokens = "optional"). Because this host runs an internet-facing PHP application that carries a near-administrative instance profile, a single SSRF flaw is sufficient to retrieve the role's temporary credentials.

Neither the instance nor its parameter group enforces TLS for client connections (no require_secure_transport = 1), and the PHP client built in user_data connects with plain mysqli_connect. Database credentials and query data may traverse the network unencrypted.
The MySQL 8.0 parameter group only sets character set options and omits require_secure_transport = 1, so the database will accept unencrypted client connections.

The master username is hard-coded to the predictable value 'admin' and the password is supplied via var.password, which is written in cleartext into Terraform state and propagated into EC2 user data. Use of managed_master_user_password / Secrets Manager would avoid persisting the secret.

Port 3306 is opened to the entire VPC CIDR rather than to the application security group. Every workload in the VPC, including unrelated or lower-trust instances, can reach the database directly, defeating network segmentation.

All protocols and ports are permitted outbound to 0.0.0.0/0 from the database security group, providing an unconstrained channel for data exfiltration or command-and-control if the database host is compromised.

No root_block_device or ebs_block_device block sets encrypted = true, so the instance volume — which contains the DB credentials written to /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc — may be stored unencrypted unless account-level EBS default encryption happens to be enabled.
